headline: Equities closed the week positive but enter the busiest week of Q2 earnings season with a live Iran re-escalation risk, June CPI due Tuesday, and Fed Chair Warsh testifying to Congress.
stance: The market absorbed a mid-week oil shock and finished Friday with modest gains — S&P 500 prior cash close 7,575, Dow 52,637, Nasdaq 26,282 — but the risk calendar ahead is dense. Tuesday lands a June CPI print the same morning the five largest US banks report and Warsh takes the Congressional hot-seat; that triple-event could reset the rate-hike pricing (markets are currently leaning toward a September hike) in either direction. Geopolitically, Trump declared the Iran ceasefire "over" on Wednesday, but Qatar-mediated talks are ongoing and Iranian media denies progress — oil and yield direction will be driven by weekend headlines.

news.head: Iran ceasefire breakdown
news.body: Trump declared the US-Iran ceasefire over at the NATO summit in Ankara; US forces carried out strikes on Iranian targets mid-week, Iran retaliated against US facilities in Kuwait and Bahrain, though Qatar negotiators were in Tehran by Friday attempting to revive talks.

news.head: SK Hynix US debut — record IPO
news.body: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix opened Friday on the Nasdaq at ~$170, roughly 14% above its $149 ADR offering price, raising $26.5 billion — the largest-ever US listing by a foreign company.

news.head: Meta AI memo lifts stock
news.body: Meta jumped ~6% Friday after a Bank of America note citing an internal memo suggested Meta is improving its AI cost structure; the stock logged its best weekly gain since early 2024.

news.head: Delta earnings disappoint
news.body: Delta Air Lines reported Q2 results; despite a top-and-bottom-line beat the stock's guidance failed to impress traders worried about fuel costs tied to the Middle East conflict.

news.head: IEA: 2026 oil demand to shrink
news.body: The International Energy Agency said world oil demand is on pace to fall 1 million barrels/day year-on-year in 2026 — the first annual decline since the Covid-19 pandemic — citing the Strait of Hormuz disruption as the main driver.

news.head: Fed semi-annual report flags inflation
news.body: The Fed's semi-annual Monetary Policy Report reiterated inflation remains elevated, citing tariffs, Middle East energy developments, and AI-driven demand; Warsh testifies to the House on Tuesday and Senate on Wednesday.

news.head: Japan yen intervention watch
news.body: USD/JPY fell back from ~162.5 to ~161.7 (prior cash close) on Friday after Japan's Finance Minister said the government would encourage domestic pension funds to raise holdings of Japanese financial assets, renewing FX-intervention speculation.

implications: Tuesday's CPI report (June) is the week's single biggest macro event — a hot number alongside Warsh's testimony could solidify September rate-hike pricing and pressure both bonds and equity valuations at a CAPE of 42.

Big-bank earnings Tuesday (JPMorgan, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Citi, Goldman) and ASML/TSM Wednesday will set the earnings-season tone — strong capital-markets revenue is expected, but forward guidance on rates and loan demand matters most.

Oil remains the swing variable: Brent prior cash close ~$76/bbl and WTI ~$71.51/bbl are well off the mid-week spike highs, but any resumption of Hormuz disruption could re-ignite the inflation/yield feedback loop that rattled markets Wednesday.

The yen (prior cash close 161.67 ¥/$) sits at a 3-year extreme (98th percentile); a softer-than-expected CPI on Tuesday historically triggers sharp yen short-cover moves — watch for volatility in USD/JPY around 8:30am Tuesday.

Positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Nasdaq 100 futures, Russell 2000 futures, and 3M SOFR — a contrarian floor across rates and equities. Speculators are also at an extended short in British Pound futures (1st percentile, 3-year low) — a contrarian-bullish lean for GBP. Offsetting that, speculators are heavily extended long in Copper futures (95th percentile) — a contrarian warning for the metal even as the spot price sits at an extreme 97th percentile. High-yield bond dealer inventory is also extended long (89th percentile) — a mild contrarian caution for credit.

watch.head: Tuesday 8:30am — June CPI
watch.body: The most important near-term data point: a reading above ~3.5% year-on-year on core CPI would likely cement a September Fed hike and send yields and the dollar higher.

watch.head: Tuesday — Big-bank earnings
watch.body: JPMorgan, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Citi, and Goldman all report before the open on Tuesday; forward loan-demand and net-interest-margin guidance will move the KBW Bank Index and the broader market.

watch.head: Tuesday/Wednesday — Warsh Congressional testimony
watch.body: Fed Chair Warsh testifies to the House Tuesday and Senate Wednesday; any explicit signal on rate-hike vs. hold will be the week's biggest Fed communication event.

watch.head: Iran/Hormuz weekend headlines
watch.body: Qatar-mediated talks are the only thing preventing a full re-escalation; a breakdown over the weekend would send oil and gold sharply higher at Sunday's open.

watch.head: ASML and TSM earnings (Wed)
watch.body: Results from semiconductor equipment giant ASML and chip foundry TSM will signal whether the AI-driven capex supercycle is intact or showing early fatigue.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield: prior cash close 4.56%; 2-year yield: prior cash close 4.21% — the yield curve is positive (10Y minus 2Y = +35 bps), a modest steepening from deeply inverted levels of 2023-24.
Real (inflation-adjusted) 10-year rate stands at 2.32% — still restrictive territory and a headwind for high-multiple growth stocks.

10-year inflation expectations (breakeven) are anchored at 2.24%, but the mid-week oil spike tested that ceiling; June CPI on Tuesday is the next read on whether tariffs and energy costs are bleeding into the broader price level.
The Fed's own semi-annual report flagged elevated inflation from tariffs, Middle East energy, and AI demand; markets are pricing roughly a 63% chance of a September quarter-point rate hike.
Financial conditions (ANFCI -0.51 z-score, STLFSI -0.72) remain easy in aggregate — credit is not yet the constraint; the constraint is inflation and geopolitics.
Bond-market volatility (MOVE index 69.5) is contained relative to 2023 levels, suggesting the Treasury market is not panicking — yet.
4-week moving average of jobless claims: 219K; most recent weekly print 215K — the labor market is cooling slowly, not cracking, consistent with the soft-landing narrative.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in 3M SOFR futures (1st percentile of 3 years) — historically a contrarian-bullish signal for rates (i.e., rates may struggle to rise further than the market fears). Speculators are also at an extended short in 3M SOFR meaning they are betting heavily on higher rates — the mirror image is a potential squeeze if CPI undershoots.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500 prior cash close: 7,575 (+0.42% Fri); Nasdaq 100 prior cash close: 26,282 (+0.29% Fri); Dow prior cash close: 52,637 (+0.29% Fri) — all three indexes closed the week in positive territory despite mid-week Iran shock.
Market breadth is healthy: 65.8% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day moving average and 68.1% above their 200-day — broad participation, not a narrow mega-cap rally.
Nvidia (+4%) and Meta (+6%) were the week's big tech winners; IBM (-2.5%) and UnitedHealth (-1.5%) were the notable laggards on Friday.
SK Hynix's $26.5bn IPO debut (up ~14% on the day) signals robust institutional appetite for AI-memory exposure heading into earnings season.
Semiconductor index (SOX) closed back above its 50-day moving average Friday after falling below it earlier in the week — technically constructive, though SOX remains ~11% below June peaks.
Cyclical rotation was visible: financials, industrials (Caterpillar, Applied Materials), and consumer discretionary led Thu/Fri while defensives lagged — consistent with a soft-landing base case.
CAPE ratio at 42.2 — stretched by any historical standard; a hawkish CPI or yield spike would pressure this multiple quickly.
Equity-credit correlation (0.70) is elevated — stocks and credit spreads are moving together, meaning a credit event would amplify an equity drawdown.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Nasdaq 100 futures (4th percentile, 3-year low) and Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile, 3-year low) — both are contrarian-bullish signals. VIX futures positioning is also at the low end (12th percentile). This means the futures market is not positioned for upside — a positive CPI surprise or Iran de-escalation could trigger a sharp squeeze higher, particularly in small-caps. Large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) is active in the setups noted below.

single_name.note: CarMax (used-auto retail) — 2 company insiders have been buying, large off-exchange block buying detected, a burst of unusual options buying, trading above its 200-day moving average, and shorts are relatively heavy at 4.4 days-to-cover (moderate squeeze risk). Highest-scoring fresh setup in Consumer Cyclical.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield credit spread: 270 bps over investment-grade; investment-grade option-adjusted spread: 76 bps — neither signals stress, but HY is wide enough to reflect geopolitical uncertainty.
Commercial paper funding spread (CPFF): 18 bps — money-market plumbing is clear, no bank funding stress.
FRA-OIS and SOFR-OIS spreads both sit at -9 bps — slightly negative, indicating the interbank lending market is well-supplied with cash and sees near-zero counterparty risk.

Bank reserves: $3,099bn — ample system liquidity; the Fed's reverse-repo facility (RRP) has effectively drained to just $0.5bn, meaning nearly all excess cash has migrated into T-bills and bank reserves.
Treasury General Account (TGA): $774bn — a large government cash buffer; drawdowns from here (ahead of debt-ceiling or spending dynamics) would inject further liquidity into the system.
M2 money supply is growing at 5.6% year-on-year and bank credit at 5.9% YoY — both consistent with an economy still running above its long-run trend.

Syndicated loan yield: 6.98% — borrowing costs for leveraged companies are elevated but stable; SLOOS data (April) shows net 8.1% of banks are tightening C&I loan standards, a mild but not alarming tightening impulse.
sections.positioning: Primary-dealer inventory in high-yield bonds is at the 89th percentile of its 3-year range — dealers are heavily long HY paper, a mild contrarian caution: if risk appetite fades on a hot CPI print, dealers may need to reduce inventory quickly, widening spreads.

single_name.note: Scorpio Tankers (crude/product tanker operator) — 2 company insiders have been buying, large off-exchange block buying and a burst of unusual options buying both active, 4.0 days-to-cover in short interest (moderate squeeze risk), trading above its 200-day moving average. Directly levered to Hormuz shipping-risk premium; signal aging at 88% weight.
